chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Mudabbir (a slave manumitted upon the owner's death), is he sold? He said, 'If his owner needs his price (to pay debts or for other needs).' And he said, 'If the slave consents, there is no harm.'

key_terms.أَ يُبَاعُ: Is he sold? (Question regarding the permissibility of selling the Mudabbir).
key_terms.الْمَمْلُوكُ: The slave (specifically the Mudabbir in this context).
key_terms.الْمُدَبَّرِ: Mudabbir: A slave whose manumission is contingent upon the death of the master.

ai.seo_question: Can a Mudabbir be sold before the owner's death?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the condition of the owner's 'need' (ihtijaj) is interpreted by Shia jurists as a relative necessity rather than absolute poverty, allowing for the sale of the Mudabbir to settle debts or fund essential needs. The inclusion of the slave's consent ensures fairness, reflecting the principle that the Mudabbir’s path to freedom should not be arbitrarily obstructed by the owner's whims, a key distinction in Usuli fiqh regarding the revocability of the tadbir contract.
